content_voiceover: This slide presents the Taiwan CML guideline for TKI discontinuation, which closely mirrors the international ELN and NCCN frameworks you just saw. Mandatory requirements are the same core elements: chronic phase disease only, a motivated patient with structured communication about relapse risk, access to high quality quantitative PCR testing, and the patient's agreement to more frequent monitoring after stopping. The minimal requirement, meaning stopping is allowed, requires first line therapy, or second line if intolerance was the only reason for switching, a typical e13a2 or e14a2 BCR ABL1 transcript, TKI duration greater than five years, or greater than four years for second generation TKIs, deep molecular response duration greater than two years, and critically, no prior treatment failure. The optimal requirement, where stopping is more strongly recommended, raises the bar to TKI duration over five years combined with an even deeper or more sustained molecular response, MR4 for over three years or MR4.5 for over two years. This Taiwan-specific guideline is useful to know for local practice patterns on boards style questions.
keypoints: Mirrors ELN and NCCN: mandatory, minimal, and optimal requirement tiers
Mandatory: chronic phase, motivated patient, quality PCR, close monitoring
Minimal: over five years TKI, over two years deep molecular response, no prior failure
Optimal: deeper or more durable response strengthens the case to stop
keypoint_voiceover: The Taiwan guideline essentially adopts the same three tier structure as ELN and NCCN. The non-negotiable mandatory items focus on disease phase and monitoring capability, the minimal requirement sets a five year therapy and two year deep response threshold with no prior treatment failure, and the optimal requirement asks for an even deeper, more durable molecular response before stopping is strongly recommended.
